title: Cloud computing
competency: Explain cloud computing, its benefits, limitations, types and the SaaS, PaaS and IaaS services.

keywords.def: Storing and accessing data and computing services (servers, storage, networking, databases, software) over the Internet, on demand.
A model where users pay only for the cloud resources they actually use.
A time when a cloud service is interrupted, so users cannot reach their data or files.
A cloud where one service provider's resources are shared across different clients, each kept logically separate.
A cloud with all resources dedicated to one organization, giving full control over security and privacy.
A combination of public and private cloud: public services in the public part, confidential data in the private part.

en.text: Cloud computing is storing and accessing data and computing services over the Internet instead of only on your own computer. Servers, storage, networking, databases and software are available on demand from a provider's data centers. Many users can be served from one data center, and they reach their data from anywhere, at any time, with an Internet connection. Gmail, Google Maps, Netflix, PayPal, Spotify and Adobe Creative Cloud are cloud-based services.

en.text: Cloud computing gives accessibility and mobility (any device, anywhere, with backup by the provider), flexibility (change resources any time and collaborate in real time), updating and scalability (the provider maintains and updates), optimized security, and controlled costs (pay as you go). Hosting a website shows the difference: buying, installing and running your own server costs much time and money, while cloud hosting needs only an upload and is ready in minutes.

en.text: Cloud computing has limitations: server downtime (and no service when the Internet is down), security and privacy risks (it is not completely safe), unclear data ownership and transparency, inflexibility when providers force their own applications and formats, little customer support, and unknown or growing costs. Weigh benefits and limitations before choosing a service.

ideas.name: Types of cloud: public, private, hybrid, community

en.text: There are four main types of cloud. A public cloud shares one provider's resources across many clients, each kept logically separate. A private cloud dedicates all resources to one organization and gives full control over security. A hybrid cloud combines both: public services in the public part, confidential data in the private part. A community cloud is shared by several organizations in the same field with common security and compliance needs, and is managed privately.

ideas.name: Cloud services: SaaS, PaaS and IaaS

en.text: The three major cloud services are SaaS, PaaS and IaaS. SaaS gives end users finished applications over the Internet by subscription, such as Google Workspace, Dropbox and Microsoft Office 365. PaaS gives developers a platform to build, test and host applications, such as Heroku, Google App Engine and Azure. IaaS rents virtual servers, storage and networks, such as AWS and Google Compute Engine. From IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, the provider manages more of the stack.
